newsitem.title: USA: Conceptus technology gets FDA clearance.
newsitem.headline: Conceptus technology gets FDA clearance.

text.p: Conceptus Inc said Wednesday the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved marketing of the company's Microgyn resectoscope safety sheath and accessories for minimally invasive urologic surgery.
The company said it is gearing up for production of the resectoscope safety sheath and accessories and anticipates launching the product in the second quarter of this year.
The approved applications include transurethral resection and ablation (non-incisional removal of tissue) within the urethra, prostate and bladder.

One of these procedures, transurethral resection of the prostate, is used to treat symptomatic, enlarged prostates, a condition known as benign prostatic hyperplasia, which affects up to 80 percent of men over the age of 50.
There are about 130,000 of these procedures performed in the United States annually, Conceptus pointed out.

The company said it plans to file a separate submission for gynecologic applications of the technology next month. These involve therapeutic hysteroscopy, a less invasive alternative to many of the over 600,000 hysterectomies performed each year in the United States.

The Microgyn resectoscope safety sheath and accessories are designed to enable surgeons to use isotonic (physiologic) irrigating solutions during the performance of electrosurgical urologic procedures to remove abnormal tissue. Currently, electrosurgical procedures can only be performed with hypotonic (low salt) irrigating solutions.
However, there are complications associated with the absorption of large amounts of hypotonic solutions including serious heart, lung, and brain disorders.
The company said the use of isotonic solutions should eliminate the incidence of these potentially catastrophic complications.
Conceptus said it is in discussions with potential distribution partners with a strong franchise in urology to market the product line for the urologic applications.
For gynecologic applications, the company plans to expand its direct sales force in the United States and use specialty distributors in markets outside the United States.
